text:
Dmitri: quick note  we saw a p99 tail bump in hosted streaming after the recent kernel selector tweak. p50 steady, p95 small shift, p99 +120ms for long seqs. sharing lab traces.

Evelyn: saw the alert. p50 ~unchanged, p95 +8ms, p99 +120ms. window ~09:10-09:40 UTC.

Ada: any KV cache churn? streaming prefixes can thrash small caches and spike tail.

Dmitri: KV miss rate up ~10% in the window. perf snapshot:
```
config: kernel=triton-microv3, microbatch=16, stream_chunk_tokens=8, flush_ms=40
metrics: p50=18ms p95=86ms p99=245ms throughput=185rps
kv: hit=88% avg_lookup=1.3ms
hotspots: many small kernel launches and extra memcpy
```

Ben: if microkernels cause many tiny launches, that often correlates with p99. What if microbatch increases?

Dmitri: microbatch=24 (other params same): p50=20ms p95=80ms p99=180ms throughput=195rps. Tail improved but p50 slightly worse for first-token.

Carla: increasing flush interval to coalesce tokens should help tail but hurts perceived-first-token. Any experiments on flush_ms?

Dmitri: flush_ms=80, chunk_tokens=8, microbatch=16 => p50=25ms p95=78ms p99=160ms throughput=172rps. p99 much better, p50 regressed.

Evelyn: product's UX team flags if p50 delta >+12ms for chat. We need a balance: drop p99 without busting perceived-first-token.

Ada: alternative: adaptive flush (immediate first-byte, buffer subsequent tokens for X ms). Keeps perceived-first-byte, reduces later kernel launches.

Ben: also consider chunk_tokens=16 with flush_ms=40. Bigger per-flush payload, fewer kernel starts but still immediate initial flush.

Dmitri: ran chunk_tokens=16 experiment: p50=20ms p95=82ms p99=170ms throughput=168rps. Good tail improvement.

Carla: kernel selection fallback to cuBLAS reduces launches but increased latency on short sequences in prior runs, right?

Dmitri: yes. cuBLAS for attention with microbatch=16 => p50=30ms p95=120ms p99=360ms. Fused path reduced launches but penalized short seq latency and memory.

Evelyn: so we want fewer launches but not at expense of short-seq latency. Adaptive flush + modest microbatch seems promising.

Dmitri: proposal: 3-arm experiment on 10% traffic: A) adaptive-flush (first immediate, followup=60ms) + microbatch=16; B) chunk_tokens=16, flush_ms=40, microbatch=16; C) kernel-heuristic=prefer-fused-if-launchs>8 + microbatch=16. Collect p50/p95/p99, perceived-first-byte, kernel-launch histogram, kv-miss, and nvprof samples for p99.

infra-bot: perf-experiment created id=exp-20260325-01 assigned to Dmitri, Carla, Ada

Ben: add microkernel-launch histogram to telemetry. correlate >N-launches -> p99 and sample nvprof when threshold exceeded.

Ada: will prototype per-prefix KV TTL (prefix_len<10 => TTL=12s) on staging to reduce repeated small-prefix refills from streaming clients.

Carla: action items: (1) run A/B for 24h, (2) add kernel-launch telemetry and tail sampler, (3) stage KV TTL patch and smoke test. Post flamegraphs to #eng-runtime.

Dmitri: uploading traces to the channel when experiments start. If regression alerts hit, ping me @Dmitri.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: perf-config/exp-20260325-01 -> 4 nodes

pm-ux: front-end note  if we enable adaptive flush, streaming UI may see slightly larger chunk sizes mid-response. PM wants p50 delta <=+8ms as acceptance while p99 should drop >=50ms.

Ben: will add launch-count histogram and a sampled tracer for requests with >10 kernel launches.

Ada: TTL patch ready behind a feature flag. Will run a small customer-scoped test on staging.

Carla: timeline: start experiments in 2h, collect 12h of data, reconvene with heatmaps and flamegraphs. Prioritize fixes that lower p99 without breaking first-token UX.

Dmitri: thanks team :rocket: everyone please watch the SLO alerts during the run and post nvprof captures for p99 offenders.
